Today’s discussion

A 50-minute review plan. Resolve the marked notation first. Use the playable opening sections of rounds 4 and 7; their later positions are not reconstructed.

0–5 min · Ask her first

Which game felt best? Where did she feel unsure? Confirm the queen exchange in round 1, Black’s move 21 in round 6, and the gaps in rounds 4 and 7.

5–17 min · Attack with a reason

Compare rounds 1 and 5. When does Ng5 create a threat? Before choosing another check, find the king’s best escape and decide whether development is stronger.

17–30 min · Notice the reply

Use the turning points in the analysis page. Ask for the opponent’s strongest check, capture, or threat before revealing the engine line.

30–42 min · Convert an advantage

Review round 2 and the confirmed part of round 6. After winning material, compare forcing moves with bringing the remaining pieces into play and keeping the king safe.

42–47 min · Defend actively

Use the recorded opening of round 7. Look for a central break before moving the same piece again. Separate a tactical necessity from a passive habit.

47–50 min · One habit to practise

Have Mishika say her own rule: “Before I move, I check their checks and captures.” Choose one position she can explain and replay without hints.
